title: POC throughput experimentation lab sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on experimental throughput tweaks: continuous batching changes, concurrency target reset, queue depth shaping and a brief KV cache behavior check. Agreed on targeted experiments and demos for next week; Redwood to run a small head-to-head with 2 quant profiles and share results. Some transcription noise on product names (Redwood dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated).
topics: cost/throughput tradeoffs and quick perf experiments
action_items: Ava: share experiment runbook + benchmark sheet (due: 2026-04-20)
Jonah: schedule controlled head-to-head runs with qprofile A/B and capture p50/p95/p99 (due: 2026-04-21)
Rachel: provide golden prompt set (50 prompts) and target success criteria for quality regression (due: 2026-04-19)
Tomas: validate network egress and confirm VPC peering metrics for test environment (due: 2026-04-22)
next_steps: Redwood to run two quantization profiles vs baseline and upload latency CSV
Customer to send production-like prompt samples and cost/latency targets
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-15 10:30 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees listed above

Summary (auto): quick lab-style sync to align on experiment matrix, check yesterday's run anomalies, and lock down next week's validation plan.

[00:00] Ava Martinez: okay good morning everyone, uh thanks for joining. we wanted to keep this pretty surgical today — a lab sync on throughput experiments. is that still the right framing Samir?

[00:23] Samir Patel: yeah that's right, quick one. we had that spike yesterday where p99 drifted out around 850 ms, trying to understand whether thats kv cache cold or just batching blowing out.

[01:05] Jonah Kim: right, so the two leads — we changed continuous batching window from 8ms to 12ms and also bumped concurrency cap from 16 to 24. early telemetry shows higher throughput but tail went up. could be a queueing interaction.

[02:12] Lena Ortiz: just to flag, our infra team saw GPU utilization bounce 90% at the same time as latency, which made us worry about saturation. Tomas and I thought maybe we were hitting model compilation jitter?

[03:01] Tomas Rivera: yeah i saw the same logs. there were a few re-compiles in the runtime, not many, but they coincide with the p99 bumps. also some tcp retransmits on the vpc peer link around that minute.

[04:00] Jonah Kim: ok two threads: one is the runtime side — continuous batch window and backpressure shape — the other is infra (vpc jitter). for runtime we can try three experiments: reduce batch window to 6ms, impose stricter queue depth limit, and test a soft-concurrency cap (eg 20 active requests) to observe loss in throughput but gain at tail.

[04:42] Rachel Wu: quick question — on the soft cap do you mean pre-queue on the klient side or at the routing tier?

[04:52] Jonah Kim: at the routing tier, basically a queue shim that enforces a token bucket so we don't push all requests into GPU queues. it'll cause backpressure to the caller but smooths bursts.

[05:20] Samir Patel: can we see a simulation of that? last time we had backpressure the app timed out clients. we need graceful fallback too.

[05:35] Ava Martinez: yes we should add a fallback policy — if queue wait exceeds 200ms we route to a cheaper variant model (quantized) or return a degraded response with confidence score. we'll include that in the runbook.

[06:12] Lena Ortiz: also want to call out KV cache warmup: yesterday we replayed a prefix-heavy workload and warmup looked slower than expected, maybe because our keys fragment across instances. is that something Redwood can instrument?

[06:37] Jonah Kim: we can add telemetry to show KV cache hit rates per instance and prefix. sometimes the metric gets labeled as K-V cash in the exporter, so just FYI — small transcription issue in dashboards.

[07:15] Rachel Wu: haha noted. on the quant experiments — which quant profiles are you planning to run? our quality bar is strict, we need p0's to verify no regressions on top-5 answers.

[07:34] Marcus Lee: we'll run two: q8a and q4x (baseline is fp16). q8a usually preserves quality well for short prompts, q4x is aggressive but cheaper. we'll compute embedding drift and token-level perplexity and check top-5 overlap.

[08:05] Samir Patel: and cost delta? we need a rough e2e token cost change to justify route fallbacks.

[08:18] Ava Martinez: Jonah, Marcus will produce a small cost matrix in the sheet. quick numbers: q8a roughly 25% cost reduction, q4x closer to 45% but with occasional quality hits depending on prompt length.

[09:10] Speaker 1: [interrupt] can i ask a naive question — why not just scale up GPU count?

[09:22] Jonah Kim: scaling is an option but it increases committed cost — if you want predictable capex we'd talk Dedicated reserved pools; otherwise we tune batching and caching for better unit economics. given Averon's burst pattern, autoscaling alone causes noisier p99s.

[10:05] Lena Ortiz: any suggestions on concurrency targets? we were using 24 but maybe that's too high.

[10:18] Jonah Kim: in this model family we saw sweet spots around 12-18 concurrent in earlier runs. beyond that the batch sizes increase but so does queue wait and serialization cost. we recommend experiments at 12, 16, 20 with metrics collected for p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.

[11:02] Tomas Rivera: can you add guidance for target GPU util? we don't want to overcommit and cause preemption.

[11:10] Jonah Kim: target 70-85% sustained; short spikes to 95% are okay if p99 stays in target. define your SLO and we can tune to it.

[12:00] Rachel Wu: about the runtime re-compiles, any knobs to avoid that during steady state?

[12:17] Marcus Lee: yes warm pools + pinned kernels option — but pinned kernels require slightly more memory. it's in the runbook as optional. it reduces jitter from JIT-like recompiles.

[13:00] Samir Patel: yesterday's anomaly — possible root causes list?

[13:10] Ava Martinez: initial triage: (1) transient vpc jitter, (2) batch window change increased tail, (3) KV cache fragmentation causing misses. we should run isolated tests to single out which one.

[14:00] Jonah Kim: proposed experiment matrix (summary): A) baseline (12ms window, conc 16), B) narrow window (6ms), C) soft token bucket + conc20, D) q8a quant profile on fallback route. run each for 1 hour with golden prompt set. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), GPU util, KV hit.

[15:12] Lena Ortiz: please add network metrics to the sheet — RTT, retrans, neighbor host errors.

[15:34] Jonah Kim: noted. we'll include system-level counters.

[16:05] Rachel Wu: re: golden prompts — i'll send 50 diversified prompts by Monday. they include long prefixes and short ones.

[16:33] Ava Martinez: great. who will run the runs on Redwood side vs customer side?

[16:40] Samir Patel: we prefer Redwood runs in a mirrored environment; we'll run one validation on our side afterwards. Tomas can help with VPC peering for data plane.

[17:05] Jonah Kim: ok Redwood to run controlled experiments in Redwood staging with your VPC peered testnet. we'll tag runs and upload CSVs to the shared drive. link: https://redwood.example.com/poc/av-8492/results (note: placeholder link).

[18:20] Speaker 2: small sidebar — are there concerns about data retention for logs?

[18:35] Ava Martinez: standard: we retain aggregated telemetry, and raw transcripts only if you enable logging; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS. will share SOC2 docs.

[19:12] Samir Patel: yes please send security pack.

[19:25] Ava Martinez: will do.

[20:00] Jonah Kim: any other open items?

[20:08] Rachel Wu: one more — can we capture latency breakdown per stage (routing, batching, model infer)?

[20:20] Jonah Kim: yes we have trace hooks; we'll include span-level breakdowns in CSVs.

[21:00] Ava Martinez: recap of next steps: run matrix A-D, Redwood to upload results and note fallback behavior, customer provide prompt set and validate. action items recorded.

[21:40] Samir Patel: perfect. thanks everyone.

[21:50] Meeting closed.
